notes.title: Potatogeddon – Official Release
notes.content: [p]The wait is over, [b]Potatogeddon[/b] is here! Step into the chaotic world of a fearless potato hero as they battle through bug labs, twisted dungeons, and dangerous arenas filled with bizarre enemies and deadly traps. Designed for both solo players and co-op duos, Potatogeddon combines fast-paced shooting, dungeon crawling, and quirky humor in one explosive package.[/p][p][/p][p]The current version of the game already includes, among others, the following mechanics:[/p][hr][/hr][h2]Key Features at Launch[/h2][h3]Weapons & Combat[/h3][list][*][p]A full [b]weapon system[/b] with unique playstyles.[/p][list][*][p][i]Blue Pulse[/i] – the classic starter weapon.[/p][/*][*][p][i]Verdant Burst[/i] – boosts max HP and strength at the cost of fire rate.[/p][/*][*][p][i]Twin Flare[/i] – fires two projectiles at once with reduced speed.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Active energy-based items[/b] that can turn the tide of battle:[/p][list][*][p][i]Phantom Shield[/i] – temporary invincibility.[/p][/*][*][p][i]Soil of Rage[/i] – unleash rapid-fire fury.[/p][/*][*][p][i]Decoytato[/i] – distracts or explodes among enemies.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Every weapon and item changes player stats, making each run unique.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]Procedural Rooms & Challenges[/h3][p]Every run offers a new labyrinth of dangers and surprises:[/p][list][*][p][b]Rootlink Rooms[/b] – destroy the core before you can damage enemies.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Pressure Plate & Platform Rooms[/b] – solve puzzles while fighting off swarms.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Lava Rooms[/b] – hazardous arenas where both players and enemies can burn.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Puzzle Rooms[/b] – environmental challenges that mix combat with clever mechanics.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]Enemies & Bosses[/h3][p]Face a bizarre lineup of mutated foes and colossal bosses:[/p][list][*][p]Face a bizarre lineup of mutated foes and colossal bosses:[/p][list][*][p]Creepy enemies like [b]Aphidoodle[/b] and flying threats like [b]Fly[/b] and [b]Green Fly[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Other twisted abominations such as [b]Microtarsa[/b], [b]Chomprax[/b], [b]Laptobettle[/b], and the armored [b]Cannon[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p]Three unique bosses, each with their own attack patterns:[/p][list][*][p][b]Beetle Prime[/b] – guardian of Level 1.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Glowgrub[/b] – the burrowing menace of Level 2.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Aphidra[/b] – a devastating insect overlord on Level 3.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]Multiplayer Co-Op[/h3][list][*][p]Team up with a friend in [b]2-player co-op[/b] (with 3–4 player support planned for the future).[/p][/*][*][p][b]Voice chat[/b] with push-to-talk, volume control, and animated mouth movement for characters.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Spectator mode[/b] for late joiners and fallen players.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Revive system[/b] – bring your teammate back into the fight by holding the action button.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]Progression & Unlocks[/h3][list][*][p][b]Game saving[/b] in both singleplayer and multiplayer.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Character stats[/b] – track your best runs, deaths, and victories.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Unlockable characters[/b] like [i]Cyclotato[/i] after completing Chapter 1.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Chapters system[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]Chapter 1 introduces the adventure.[/p][/*][*][p]Chapter 2 spans six levels and unlocks Chapter 3 – an endless challenge for hardcore players.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]Extra Features[/h3][list][*][p][b]Polish language support[/b] alongside English.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Shops with randomized prices[/b], offering items and upgrades mid-run.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Optimized maps and performance[/b] – no more wasted rendering, smoother gameplay even at higher levels.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Enhanced audio & visual polish[/b] – footsteps, explosions, lava effects, voice chat animations, and more.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr]

notes.title: DevLog #01: Level Generation
notes.content:
Hey there, fellow spud warriors!

In our very first DevLog for Potatogeddon, we’re pulling back the curtain on one of the game’s core systems: procedurally generated levels.

Our fearless potato hero isn’t wandering through some ancient ruins – he’s breaking into a heavily fortified, high-tech base run by potato beetles and other crop-devouring pests. These enemies are on a mission to wipe out all potato crops on Earth – and you’re the last line of defense!


[h2]Random, but with structure[/h2]
Each level in Potatogeddon is made up of randomly generated rooms, with their number increasing the deeper you go. For example:

Level 1: between 7 and 9 rooms
Level 3: between 14 and 18 rooms

This ensures each run feels fresh, with a new layout to explore and conquer.

At this stage of development, all rooms are square-shaped and identical in size, which helps us focus on core mechanics and overall balance. But in the future, we plan to introduce different room shapes and sizes and even adjust layouts based on the number of players. Expect more environmental variety and complexity as the base grows more sinister!

As for how many levels the full game will contain – and how big the later levels will get – we haven’t locked that down yet. The numbers are still being tested and tweaked as we shape the overall difficulty curve and pacing. But one thing's for sure: things will get wild and intense the deeper you go.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45464957/29b68fbef6c048bc517716d1f7ba9238576b61c5.png[/img]


[h2]Room types you’ll encounter[/h2]
Your infiltration journey will take you through various room types, each with a different function:

[b]Start Room[/b] – your entry point. Calm and secure, with no enemies or traps. A quiet moment before the storm.

[b]Enemy Room[/b] – once entered, all exits are sealed and enemies spawn. Defeat all threats to move forward. Expect heavy resistance.

[b]Shop Room[/b] – use the seeds you collect (the in-game currency) to upgrade your abilities or buy gear. A must-visit if you want to keep up with the base’s escalating defense systems.

[b]Reward Room [/b]– find a random item that might help you win, upgrade, or heal your character.

[b]Boss Room[/b] – defeat the boss to move deeper into the facility. Each has unique abilities and deadly tech.

Each level is built using a consistent structure, it always includes a Start Room, a Boss Room, and several Enemy Rooms. The Shop Room and Reward Room are optional – not every level will have them, so if you spot one, make sure to take advantage of it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45464957/83c4f89f8d5403c28e1bfd74f0845f916e643289.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45464957/a94fc2918632266a4d66e83864482c4358fb5b83.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45464957/1f7bcb00258730b65b9f20db26300511e37ca790.png[/img]

This is just the start – in future DevLogs, we’ll dive into combat, weapons, enemies and more.

Let us know what you think of our level generation system – and if there's anything else you'd like to see in the next update!

Stay stealthy, stay spuddy! 🥔
